title: The Glaze That Crawled
story: Nils drew the bowl from the kiln and saw the glaze had crawled, leaving a ring of bare clay. Classmates told him to stop, because the flaw looked planned to anyone who had not seen the sketch. He mixed a second coat and fired again, knowing extra heat might slump the foot. Stopping at an attractive accident would teach his hands to prize luck over the form he intended. The second firing held. The ring vanished and the foot stayed true. He kept a photograph of the flaw as a record of when he nearly let a mistake set the standard.

vocabulary.definition: The oven used to fire pottery
The glassy coating on the bowl
Lose its shape under too much heat
A spell of baking in the kiln

quiz.question: What did Nils see on the bowl fresh from the kiln?
options: A ring of bare clay where the glaze had crawled
A foot that had already slumped
A photograph stuck to the rim
A crack that split the bowl in two
quiz.correctAnswer: A ring of bare clay where the glaze had crawled
quiz.explanation: The glaze had crawled, leaving a ring of bare clay.
quiz.supportingSentence: Nils drew the bowl from the kiln and saw the glaze had crawled, leaving a ring of bare clay.

quiz.question: What danger did the extra heat carry?
options: It might slump the foot
It might erase the clay itself
It might cool the kiln at once
It might decorate the other pots
quiz.explanation: He knew the extra heat might slump the foot.
quiz.supportingSentence: He mixed a second coat and fired again, knowing extra heat might slump the foot.

quiz.question: Why does the class treat the bowl as possibly finished?
options: Someone who missed the sketch could take the flaw as intentional
The kiln had no power left for another try
The foot had already collapsed
He had promised the class he would stop
quiz.correctAnswer: Someone who missed the sketch could take the flaw as intentional
quiz.explanation: They say the flaw looked planned to anyone who had not seen the sketch.
quiz.supportingSentence: Classmates told him to stop, because the flaw looked planned to anyone who had not seen the sketch.

quiz.question: What does crawled describe in the kiln?
options: The coating drew back and left clay showing
The bowl walked across the floor
The surface matched the sketch exactly
The oven cooled before it was lit
quiz.correctAnswer: The coating drew back and left clay showing
quiz.explanation: Crawled describes the glaze pulling back and leaving bare clay.
quiz.supportingSentence: Nils drew the bowl from the kiln and saw the glaze had crawled, leaving a ring of bare clay.

quiz.question: Why save a picture of the flaw and still not treat it as the piece?
options: To remember the temptation without letting it become the goal
To sell the picture in place of the bowl
To prove the second firing failed
To teach the class to copy the bare ring
quiz.correctAnswer: To remember the temptation without letting it become the goal
quiz.explanation: The photograph records the moment he nearly let a mistake set the standard, without becoming the work itself.
quiz.supportingSentence: He kept a photograph of the flaw as a record of when he nearly let a mistake set the standard.
